classification_policy.required_for_v1: The design disposition must be represented in issue #39 and every stated implementation/release obligation must be satisfied before the autonomous MVP, unless a reviewed split moves an exact non-critical remainder after v1.
classification_policy.planned_after_v1: The capability is explicitly inactive in v1, remains mandatory for the full program, and starts at its recorded activation trigger after the autonomous MVP.
classification_policy.intentionally_deferred: Allowed only with an immutable external blocker or explicit user decision, complete risk/owner/return trigger, and no claim of full completion.
classification_policy.full_program_rule: The program continues after the autonomous MVP until all planned_after_v1 work is complete; intentionally_deferred is not completion without a later explicit user disposition.
classification_policy.evolution_rule: Any new or split issue outside the pinned inventory requires a successor matrix version, refreshed issue inventory, and full panel before it can become required_for_v1 or release-blocking.

An Epic's own integration acceptance — every answer to any acceptance packet of the Epic, accept or refuse, re-asks included, and every IntegrationAuthorizationRecord of its scope, which autoskd recognizes at commit by the kind of request each decision answers (acceptance_missing at accept_staging), not by its payload — never enters the Epic's relevant authority projection or its dependency or intent head: committing them moves the global authority and nonce heads, kept for integrity, and integration_authorization_head, never a head the record names, and any other decision — a later one revoking or replacing an acceptance decision or record included — enters them as before, so an acceptance does not move what it accepts (docs/contracts/integration-authorization.md §3, ADR-103).

The helper runs as the installing user, a process of its own with its own socket, intents, journal and nonces (docs/contracts/platform-support.md §5a, ADR-102): it is the only writer of refs/autosk/** by protocol, its expected-old compare-and-swap and preflight find a protected ref the installing user's own tools moved or packed and never overwrite or adopt it, and its Git reads run with `--no-replace-objects`. The ref-custody policy's committed example, which predates ADR-102, changes only when this issue signs the wire goldens it binds again; the probe behind `security.ref_custody` is #13's with this issue.

Model launch is this issue's under the model account (ADR-102): model launch under the model account, where the launch path starts every model process, and every check that runs code a model wrote, as `autosk-model` through the mechanism the privileged install sets up (docs/contracts/platform-support.md §5b), kills a timed-out model process tree whole through that mechanism, reads a provider session from the model's session directory only as untrusted input, creates each model worktree as the installing user with its directories setgid and group-writable for the worktree group, its gitfile at 0644 and its config.worktree pinning core.hooksPath=/dev/null and core.fsmonitor=false, hands a model step what it needs from the project's history, which the model account cannot open, and runs every Git command for a model worktree with the per-worktree Git directory and the work tree named explicitly and hooks, fsmonitor and submodule recursion off, so that a repository a model plants is never followed, and model launch only through the dispatch gate, which the launch path calls before every model launch, the workflow's first agent step included, and whose refusal launches nothing; the gate holds the workflow to its model-step checks, `daemon.capabilities_pinned`, `security.signer_boundary` and `security.model_account`, and its required sets and checks are #34's (docs/contracts/doctor-report.md §7).

records.issue_title: [P1] Реализовать autosk-native Autobuild Generator/Evaluator workflow

The unattended acceptance the run contract's approved_auto_policy names — a policy that accepts at accept_staging without the person at the stop — is this issue's own post-v1 design work, which a successor panel reviews before any of it is built: under the v1 binding (`autoPolicyAcceptance`, #9's) an auto-policy adds no autonomy, because it only removes the wait after the person has signed that exact post-aggregate staging identity, so an unattended acceptance needs a different binding — something the person signs before the identity exists — and a narrow exception, for that path alone, to the rule that no policy issues the IntegrationAuthorizationRecord (docs/contracts/integration-authorization.md §1); `autoPolicyAcceptance` cannot admit it, and no v1 graph edge reaches an acceptance without the person (ADR-103).
records.verification_expectation: Post-v1 E2E covers immutable contract, budgets/no-progress, generator/evaluator independence, crash recovery and normal gates.

records.issue_title: [P1] Перенести bounded loop protocol и четыре обязательных escalation trigger
records.rationale: A bounded iteration controller prevents repeated no-op attempts and forces escalation on invalid premise, out-of-scope decisions or missing permission.
records.classification_risk: Without it implementation can exhaust provider budgets or mutate scope while appearing to make progress.
records.activation_trigger: Active in the v1 program; execute when all listed dependencies and the current phase gate are satisfied.
records.design_obligation_before_issue_39: Include iteration schema, progress identity, four triggers and crash-safe counters in the v1 design.
records.implementation_obligation_before_mvp: Implement the controller across planning repair, debugging, implementation, fix and verification support. The review cap `artifact_review_round` bounds each artifact's review cycle: it counts the artifact's narrow and full-panel NOT_PASS rounds as one count against 10, since the cycle's verified boundary — the artifact's PASS published, `publish_artifact_pass -> select_next` — from the baseline the factory records at that crossing; no decision or anchor rebuild opens a cycle, and the count never falls below the rounds since the last verified PASS publication, though a resume out of a status park at the boundary step counts as a crossing and a PASS published under binding drift closes none (narrow re-review of 12c); counted per task, it would end an Epic's autonomous planning at its fourth artifact on a host that admits no cap decision (ADR-104, review of 12c). The code review cap and the verification repair cycle's count per task: the repair cycle is bounded absolutely by the workflow graph's cap `verification_repair_round`, which counts `t_416` (`verify -> fix`) against a limit of 10 over the durable takings and parks with `verification_cap`, enforced by the factory's cap term (ADR-104). The controller's own budgets, pinned before dispatch per Ticket and per run, run inside those caps and never past them, and a resume past a cap into another round — past the repair cap `fix`, `verify` or `rebuild_code_anchor` — is the user's, one round per recorded cap decision (ADR-099).
records.verification_expectation: Tests cover repeated errors, new hypotheses, no-op edits, each escalation trigger, provider retry distinction and crash/cap behavior.

records.issue_title: [P1] Добавить `autosk-flow doctor` для fail-fast проверки проекта, runtime и recovery state
records.rationale: A single doctor command reuses preflight checks and makes complex capability/recovery failures diagnosable before side effects.
records.classification_risk: Without it release readiness and operator recovery fragment across opaque runtime failures.
records.activation_trigger: Active in the v1 program; execute when all listed dependencies and the current phase gate are satisfied.
records.design_obligation_before_issue_39: Define read-only check registry, required check sets, provenance/expiry and JSON output in the v1 design.
records.implementation_obligation_before_mvp: Implement doctor for autoskd, locks, filesystem, provider, Git/delivery, clearance, evidence and recovery state. The `security.signer_boundary` check is this issue's: the signer boundary probe passes only once the daemon reports #4's signer (ADR-090). The `daemon.capabilities_pinned` check is this issue's with #11 and #18 (ADR-097): the daemon capability check hands the daemon's meta.capabilities report to requireDaemonCapabilities and decides nothing itself, and is unverifiable where doctor has no report. So is the dispatch gate before any model launch, the second caller of the check library (docs/contracts/doctor-report.md §7): the required sets and the admission that hold each registered workflow to its set, every model-step check included, before its first agent step runs; the call before each launch sits in #18's launch path (ADR-102). The `security.model_account` check is this issue's with #11, #13 and #18 (ADR-102): the doctor registers it and the dispatch gate before any model launch requires it, and #13's probe decides it. The doctor registers `security.ref_custody` too, which every workflow that reaches a step asking the ref-custody helper requires (derived from the graph), and the probe of #13 with #5 decides it.
records.verification_expectation: Tests cover clean and degraded projects, no-write behavior, redaction, open operations and partial provider/network outage.

records.issue_title: [P2] Расширить autosk extension SDK типизированным write API и убрать CLI из correctness-critical paths
records.rationale: A complete typed extension write API is a post-MVP control-plane improvement when the accepted v1 primitives can be proven through narrower daemon APIs.

records.owner: autosk upstream and extension SDK maintainers

records.implementation_obligation_before_mvp: No implementation before MVP. If a v1 atomic guarantee cannot be met, record an explicit user decision, split the exact typed primitive into a successor matrix, classify it required_for_v1, and pass a new full panel before implementation. The daemon primitives the v1 preflight requires are not this issue's: they are carried by #4, #9 and #18 through narrower daemon methods (ADR-092), and this issue later exposes them through the typed SDK.
records.verification_expectation: Post-v1 tests cover CAS, idempotency, transaction failure, capability scope, daemon restart and CLI/SDK semantic parity.
